{{short description|Finnish physicist}}
'''Pirkko Eskola''' is a Finnish physicist. She discovered the chemical elements [[Rutherfordium]] and [[Dubnium]] whilst working at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].

== Research ==
Eskola was a student of {{ill|Matti Nurmia|fi}} at the [[University of Helsinki]]. She worked on heavy ion physics.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P8Y5AAAAIAAJ&q=pirkko+eskola+physics|title=Studies of alpha-active nuclei using a recoil spectrometer|last=Leino|first=Matti|date=1983|publisher=University of Helsinki|isbn=9789514531439|language=en}}</ref> In 1961 Eskola demonstrated that the half-life of [[Nobelium]] was 25 seconds.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yP63CgAAQBAJ&dq=pirkko+eskola&pg=PA249|title=The Transuranium People: The Inside Story|last1=Albert|first1=Ghiorso|last2=C|first2=Hoffman Darleane|last3=T|first3=Seaborg Glenn|date=2000-01-21|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9781783262441|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=July 1969|title=CERN‐Serpukhov Collaboration Yields Data on Particle Yields|journal=Physics Today|language=en|volume=22|issue=7|pages=71|doi=10.1063/1.3035682|issn=0031-9228|bibcode=1969PhT....22g..71.}}</ref> Eskola joined [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in 1968 and stayed until 1972. She worked with [[Albert Ghiorso]], [[James Andrew Harris]] and her husband, {{ill|Kari Eskola|fi}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://newscenter.lbl.gov/2011/01/12/ghiorso-tributes/|title=Tributes to Albert Ghiorso {{!}} Berkeley Lab|date=2011-01-12|work=News Center|access-date=2018-08-08|language=en-US}}</ref> In 1969 she was part of the team that discovered [[Rutherfordium]] by bombarding [[californium]]-249 with [[Carbon-12]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nara.getarchive.net/topics/pirkko+eskola|title=Lawrence Radiation Laboratory's team that reported the positive identification of two isotopes of element 104, Rutherfordium. Left to right: Matti Nurmia, Jim Harris, Kari and Pirkko Eskola, and Albert Ghiorso. XBB6903-01735 [Photographer: Donald Cooksey] - Lawrence Radiation Laboratory's team that reported the positive identification of two isotopes of element 104, Rutherfordium. Left to right: Matti Nurmia, Jim Harris, Kari and Pirkko Eskola, and Albert Ghiorso. XBB6903-01735 [Photographer: Donald Cooksey] {{!}} U.S. National Archives, Pirkko eskola|website=U.S. National Archives|language=en|access-date=2018-08-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hlz-BAAAQBAJ&dq=pirkko+eskola+rutherfordium&pg=PA44|title=Actinides in Perspective: Proceedings of the Actinides—1981 Conference, Pacific Grove, California, USA, 10-15 September 1981|last=Edelstein|first=Norman M.|date=2013-09-11|publisher=Elsevier|isbn=9781483190518|language=en}}</ref> In 1970 she discovered [[Dubnium]] using the Heavy Ion Linear Accelerator, bombarding a target of californium-249 with [[nitrogen]] nuclei.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D_M2AQAAMAAJ&dq=pirkko+eskola+finnish&pg=PA177|title=University Bulletin: A Weekly Bulletin for the Staff of the University of California|last=(System)|first=University of California|date=1969|publisher=Office of Official Publications, University of California|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ghiorso|first1=Albert|last2=Nurmia|first2=Matti|last3=Eskola|first3=Kari|last4=Harris|first4=James|last5=Eskola|first5=Pirkko|date=1970-06-29|title=New Element Hahnium, Atomic Number 105|journal=Physical Review journal|last1=Eskola|first1=Pirkko|last2=Eskola|first2=Kari|last3=Nurmia|first3=Matti|last4=Ghiorso|first4=Albert|date=1970-09-01|title=Alpha Decay of $^{255}\mathrm{No}$ and $^{257}\mathrm{No}$|journal=Physical Review C|volume=2|issue=3|pages=1058–1062|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.2.1058|bibcode=1970PhRvC...2.1058E}}</ref> She went on to work on beta-unstable [[Alpha particle]] emitting nuclei.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TiHlBwAAQBAJ&dq=pirkko+eskola+finland+kari&pg=PA102|title=Atomic Masses and Fundamental Constants $^{261}\mathrm{Ha}$ and $^{262}\mathrm{Ha}$|journal=Physical Review C|volume=4|issue=5|pages=1850–1855|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.4.1850|bibcode=1971PhRvC...4.1850G}}</ref> Using [[Alpha-particle C|volume=7|issue=1|pages=280–289|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.7.280|bibcode=1973PhRvC...7..280E|url=https://cloudfront.escholarship.org/dist/prd/content/qt0577d996/qt0577d996.pdf}}</ref>

Her husband, Kari Eskola, was a professor of physics at the University of Helsinki.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.lbl.gov/today/2005/Jul/11-Mon/ghiospeakers-jump.html|title=Today at Berkeley Lab: Al Ghiorso's 90th Birthday Symposium -- A Roster of Stellar Speakers|website=www2.lbl.gov|access-date=2018-08-08}}</ref> She went on to have a career in science education.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://elektra.helsinki.fi/suunni.html|title=ELEKTRA - projektisuunnitelma|website=elektra.helsinki.fi|access-date=2018-08-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ercim.eu/publication/Ercim_News/enw25/alkula.html|title=A Web Publishing Project at VTT Information Service|website=www.ercim.eu|access-date=2018-08-08}}</ref> She was an editor of the Finnish Physical Society journal ''Physica Fennica''.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=53csAAAAIAAJ&q=pirkko+eskola+physics|title=Physica Fennica: Collected Reprints|date=1973|language=en}}</ref> Eskola was a member of the [[American Physical Society]] Committee for Women in Physics.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=taTvAAAAMAAJ&q=pirkko+eskola+physics|title=Women in physics: a roster|last=Physics|first=American Physical Society Committee on Women in|date=1972|publisher=Published for the American Physical Society by the American Institute of Physics|language=en}}</ref>
